questions.prompt: A customer submits your order form and it says "saved", but nothing appears in your list. Which part is most likely at fault?
options: Hosting, because Vercel has taken the whole site offline for a while
The front end, because the page design looks different on a phone
The database, because the order was not stored where it should be
GitHub, because the latest version of the code was never committed
questions.explanation: The page worked and the link opened, so it is not the front end or hosting. "Saved" but missing points at the database, or the rules on it.

questions.prompt: What makes something a web app rather than a website?
options: It saves information and responds to who is using it
It is built with Claude Code instead of written by hand
It is hosted on Vercel rather than on a different host
It has more than five pages and a menu to move between
questions.explanation: A website shows everyone the same thing. An app remembers things, like orders or sign-ins, and responds to the person using it.

questions.prompt: What does plan mode in Claude Code do?
options: It writes the whole app at once and then explains what it built
It picks the cheapest tools for the job and then installs them for you
It turns your brief into a finished design you can show a client
It reads and proposes a plan, but changes no files until you approve
questions.explanation: In plan mode Claude Code can read and think but cannot edit anything. You approve the plan before any code is written.

questions.prompt: Your site looks like every other AI-built site: a purple gradient, a centred headline and three boxes with icons. What fixes it most reliably?
options: Ask Claude Code to make the whole page look more modern and unique
Write down your never list, colours and fonts before building
Buy a website template and paste your own words into it
Add more animation so the page feels more premium and new
questions.explanation: A vague request gets the average look again. Deciding first, in writing, gives Claude Code your real colours and fonts and a list of what to avoid, every time it builds a page.

questions.prompt: You pushed a change and the Vercel build failed. What happens to your live site?
options: It goes offline until you fix the error and push again
It shows the error message to every visitor who opens it
It keeps showing the last version that built successfully
It switches over to the version still running on your laptop
questions.explanation: A failed build never replaces the live site. Visitors keep seeing the last working version while you fix it.

options: A request to Vercel asking it to publish your site
A copy of your site sent to a customer for review
A saved version of your code you can go back to
A message to Claude Code asking it to check work
questions.explanation: A commit is a saved version. Asking Claude Code to commit and push after every working step means a bad change only costs you one step.

questions.prompt: Which Supabase key must never appear in a web page or a screenshot?
options: The secret key, because it ignores every rule on every table
The publishable key, because it lets anyone change your data
The project URL, because it shows where your database lives
The anon key, because it can delete your whole project fast
questions.explanation: The secret key (service_role on older projects) has full access and bypasses RLS. The publishable key is designed to be used in the browser.

questions.prompt: You add your Supabase keys in Vercel's Environment Variables, but the live site still cannot reach the database. What is the most likely reason?
options: The keys only work on your laptop and cannot be used online
You need to delete the project in Vercel and import it again
Supabase blocks every request that comes from a Vercel site
The change only applies to a new deployment, so redeploy it
questions.explanation: Environment variable changes apply to new deployments only. Redeploy the latest deployment and the site picks up the keys.

questions.prompt: Which bug report is most likely to get a fix in one try?
options: "The site is broken on all our phones, please fix it for me."
"Order page, Android, tapped date: calendar half off-screen."
"Something is wrong with the order form, it looks strange."
"Make the whole site work better on every kind of device."
questions.explanation: Say where, what you did, what happened and what you expected, with a screenshot. Vague reports get vague fixes.

questions.prompt: Your form is blocked by Supabase and will not save. What should you do?
options: Fix the RLS rule so it allows exactly what BUILD.md says
Switch RLS off on that table so the form can save the orders
Move the secret key into the page so it has full access
Make a new table without any rules and save orders there
questions.explanation: Never switch RLS off or use the secret key to get round it. If something is blocked, the rule is wrong, so fix the rule.
